stances.claim: (Miguel) The word family instantly spurs memories of magnificent and kind faces -- memories of feelings so strong I can almost relive them; because where I stand is where they put me; I am here today because of them and will forever be grateful

(Miguel) The first memory is of Papa -- sitting on his lap pretending to play driver as we entered the gate of my parents' love nest in Alabang, newly married, laughing as we honked the horn; the memories abruptly stop there because we lost Papa to a car accident when I was just two years old

(Miguel) From there, life was populated by one of the most plaguing (and sometimes useless) questions in the English language -- 'What if?' What if I grew up with him by my side? What if he were there during father's day at school? What if he were there to see me graduate from UP (also his alma mater)? It is like talking to a closed door, shouting at it, aimlessly hoping for it to open

(Miguel) Mom always said 'When God closes doors, He opens new windows' -- while I was shouting 'what if' at closed doors, blessings were pouring through the windows God opened for us; these blessings came in the form of my family -- Tito Manu, Tito Paco, and Lolo Lito filling father's-day absence; lolos and lolas, aunts and uncles both on Sandejas and Panganiban sides rushing to Mom's broken-hearted side

(Miguel) Mom is my stronghold -- the strongest root keeping me grounded to what is good and rational; the strength of a mother will forever be greater than any superpower; God answered Mom's 'what ifs' too -- He gave her Alex, my stepfather, who helped her put the pieces of her heart back together; how many people are lucky enough to find true love twice in their life?

(Miguel) God gave me: parents that raised me to the best of their abilities -- role models in their own trials and triumphs; three sets of grandparents as models of perfect patriarchs and matriarchs -- pillars of love, support and family; aunts and uncles to be the older brothers and sisters I never had -- sources of strength and inspiration; and hopefully someday children with whom I can share everything I have learned

(Miguel, close) There will always be what ifs -- but suddenly, the answers do not seem so important anymore; God already answered them through my family; God was not selfish when He took Papa to Heaven -- He handpicked Papa from His earthly garden because He needed him a bit earlier than planned; family is the ultimate proof that God loves us, and in the end, proof that everything will be okay

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban explains the CBCP invited him to speak during the Asian Conference on the Family -- but CJ thought the audience would be better off hearing the real-life experience of the young like grandson Miguel P. Sandejas. Since Christmas is a season for the family, CJ shares Miguel's talk, slightly shortened to fit the space. Miguel begins: "The word family instantly spurs memories of faces in my head, as I am sure it does yours. Magnificent and kind faces. It spurs memories of feelings so strong that I can almost relive them right now, from where I stand. Because where I stand is where they put me. And I am here today because of them and I will forever be grateful for that." The first memory: "When I was very young, I remember sitting on the lap of Papa pretending to play driver as we entered the gate of my parents love nest in Alabang. They were newly married back then. I remember sitting on his lap and laughing as we honked the horn. The memories of my father abruptly stop there. This is because we lost Papa to a car accident when I was just two years old. From there, my life was populated by one of the most plaguing (and sometimes useless) questions in the English language -- I started to ask: What if? What if I grew up with him by my side, would life be different? What if he were there during fathers day celebrations at school? What if he were there to see me graduate from the University of the Philippines (also his alma mater)? This is where the question what if becomes useless. There is never an answer. It is like talking to a closed door, shouting at it, aimlessly hoping for it to open." The second memory is an eagle-eye view of family -- how, unseemingly, God answered Miguel's questions; how God carried Mom and Miguel through all of these years. Of course He would never abandon us. He would never abandon any of us. Had Papa been around, life would have been different. Mom always said that when God closes doors, He opens new windows. While Miguel was shouting what-if at closed doors, blessings were pouring through the windows God opened for us -- these blessings flooded through and rushed through every nook and cranny they could find, in the form of family. Papa's absence at father's day was filled by Tito Manu, Tito Paco, and Lolo Lito. Miguel's graduation day was celebrated with many people who loved him. Family filled in the empty spaces left by loss -- uplifted us and kept us going even when we thought we could not; rushed to Mom's side when she stood there broken by the death of her husband -- lolos and lolas, aunts and uncles both on the Sandejas and Panganiban sides -- they helped her hold on to the pieces of her broken heart. Mom is Miguel's stronghold -- the strongest root keeping him grounded to what is good and rational. He admires her for keeping herself together through loss, for keeping herself together for him and raising him the way she did. In Miguel's opinion, no one should ever be put through the pain of love and loss; however, the strength of a mother will forever be greater than any superpower anyone can ever have. Mom asked her own what-ifs at that time -- and God answered them too. He gave her Alex, Miguel's stepfather, who helped her put the pieces of her heart back together -- he offered his life and forever support to her in marriage; how many people are lucky enough to find true love twice in their life? He also gave her a second son, Miguel's brother Rafa, who is a Godsend as well. Our family is complete again, even better and stronger than it used to be. The last thing Miguel shares is what he has taken away: in the absence of a father, he realized the presence of many other prominent figures. God gave him parents that raised him to the best of their abilities -- role models in their own trials and triumphs. God gave him three sets of grandparents that serve as models of perfect patriarchs and matriarchs -- pillars of love, support and family. God gave him aunts and uncles to be the older brothers and sisters he never had -- sources of strength and inspiration at any given time. One day Miguel hopes He will give him children with whom to share everything he has learned. There will always be what-ifs. But suddenly, the answers do not seem so important anymore. God already answered them through Miguel's family. There are many times in our lives that we ask why God takes away. God was not selfish when He took Papa to Heaven; Miguel believes that He handpicked Papa from His earthly garden because He needed him a bit earlier than planned. He was taught to accept this unconditionally. He realizes now that life always goes on, even after death. God will always be there -- in the form of Family, in the form of Love, a love that is pure, honest and unfaltering. Family is the ultimate proof that God loves us, and in the end, proof that everything will be okay.
